analysis.title: Ingersoll Rand Inc. (IR): Raising out year estimates on order strength
key_insights: IR reported 3Q26 adj. segment EBITDA of $596mn (excluding IEEPA refunds) vs Visible Alpha consensus of $594mn, in line. Better margins in P&ST were offset by lower margins in IT&S.
Organic orders were +18.2% vs +1.6% in 2Q. IT&S organic orders were +22.1% (flat in 2Q) and P&ST orders were +4.2% (+7.4% in 2Q). Book-to-bill was 1.14x.
Organic revenue growth was +3.9%: IT&S +3.5% and P&ST +5.5%.

Management maintained the FY26 EBITDA guide of $2,130mn to $2,190mn but now expects to finish in the lower half of the range. Organic growth guidance was raised to +2% to +3.5% from +1% to +3%. FY26 EPS is expected at $3.58-$3.70.
GS sees a broadening industrial recovery. IT&S short-to-medium-cycle orders accelerated to mid-single-digit growth, and long-cycle orders grew over 20% excluding the $195mn data center award.

The $195mn APAC award is IR's first major data center win. It is a modular, containerized backup power generation solution that integrates third-party generators with IR's own content. GS calls it a proof point for using existing engineered-to-order capabilities in a new end market.
Repeat data center orders and margin upside from more proprietary content remain to be demonstrated. Lower initial data center margins could partly offset the benefit to FY27 growth visibility.
GS expects sequential margin improvement in 4Q26 and further expansion in 2027, supported by improving price-cost, volume growth, productivity and easing China pricing pressures.
GS moved FY26/FY27/FY28 EBITDA estimates to $2,150mn/$2,325mn/$2,465mn from $2,155mn/$2,295mn/$2,435mn, reflecting near-term margin pressure and stronger FY27 growth.
Buy rating maintained. The 12-month price target was raised to $91 from $87 (13.7% upside from $80.05) by rolling the Q5-Q8 EBITDA forward at an unchanged 16.0x target multiple.

market_movers.rationale: PT raised to $91 from $87 by rolling Q5-Q8 EBITDA forward at an unchanged 16.0x multiple. Orders strength improves FY27 growth visibility, while near-term margins stay under pressure.
